paragraphs.title: Laws concerning the man with a discharge and uncleanness

easy.question: Who spoke to Moses and Aaron at the beginning of the passage?
answers: The Lord
The Israelites
The priests
easy.explanation: The first verse says, “The Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron.”

easy.question: To whom were Moses and Aaron commanded to speak?
answers: Pharaoh
The children of Israel
The priests only
easy.explanation: They were commanded to speak these instructions to the children of Israel.

easy.question: What is said about a man who has a discharge from his body?
answers: He is clean
He is a king
He is unclean
easy.explanation: The verse explicitly says that because of his discharge he is unclean.

medium.question: What two conditions does the passage describe as signs of the discharge?
answers: His body runs with the discharge or is stopped from it
He is in pain or tired
He drinks or eats
medium.explanation: The verse describes his flesh running with the discharge or being stopped from the discharge.

medium.question: What is the order of events in the passage?
answers: Israel speaks to the Lord, and then the Lord speaks
The Lord speaks to Moses and Aaron, and they are told to speak to Israel
Aaron speaks to Moses, and Moses speaks to the Lord
medium.explanation: First the Lord speaks to Moses and Aaron, then commands them to speak to the Israelites.

medium.question: What does the phrase “his flesh run with his issue” describe?
answers: He is healed
His body is completely closed
Fluid is flowing from his body
medium.explanation: The phrase describes a discharge flowing from the man’s body.

challenge.question: What does the repeated wording “any man” emphasize?
answers: The law applies to every man who has such a discharge
The law applies to only two men
The law applies only to leaders
challenge.explanation: The wording emphasizes that every man in this condition is included.

challenge.question: Why does verse 3 describe the way the discharge appears?
answers: To tell about two different men
To clarify the ways the discharge may be evident in the body
To describe Israel’s journey
challenge.explanation: The verse gives two possible ways the discharge may appear, clarifying the uncleanness being discussed.

challenge.question: What does “this shall be his uncleanness” refer to?
answers: Every possible illness
Moses’ position
The signs of the discharge just described
challenge.explanation: The phrase refers to the discharge flowing from the body or being stopped from it.

questions.question: What does the repeated wording “any man” emphasize?
answers: The law applies to every man who has such a discharge
The law applies to only two men
The law applies only to leaders
questions.explanation: The wording emphasizes that every man in this condition is included.

answers: To tell about two different men

questions.explanation: The verse gives two possible ways the discharge may appear, clarifying the uncleanness being discussed.

answers: Every possible illness

The signs of the discharge just described
questions.explanation: The phrase refers to the discharge flowing from the body or being stopped from it.

easy.question: What becomes unclean if the man with the discharge lies on it?
answers: The bed
Only his clothes
Only his hands
easy.explanation: The passage says that every bed on which he lies is unclean.

easy.question: What must a person do after touching the bed of the man with the discharge?
answers: Wait without doing anything
Wash his clothes and bathe in water
Break the bed
easy.explanation: The verse commands him to wash his clothes and bathe in water.

easy.question: What must be done to an earthen vessel touched by the man with the discharge?
answers: It must be washed with water
It must be kept until evening
It must be broken
easy.explanation: Verse 12 says that an earthen vessel he touches must be broken.

medium.question: What do a person who touches the man’s body and a person upon whom he spits have in common?
answers: Both wash their clothes, bathe, and remain unclean until evening
Both must break an earthen vessel
Both become clean immediately without bathing
medium.explanation: In both cases, the person must wash, bathe, and remain unclean until evening.

medium.question: In the phrase “every saddle whereon he rides,” what is the saddle?
answers: The man’s clothing
The seat or equipment used for riding
The water in which he bathes
medium.explanation: The context shows that it is something used as a riding seat.

medium.question: What happens to someone who carries an object that touched the man with the discharge?
answers: He becomes clean immediately
He must break the object
He washes his clothes, bathes, and is unclean until evening
medium.explanation: Verse 10 gives these instructions for anyone who carries such an object.

challenge.question: What distinction between earthen and wooden vessels appears in verse 12?
answers: The earthen vessel is broken, and the wooden vessel is rinsed with water
Both are broken
The wooden vessel is burned, and the earthen vessel is washed
challenge.explanation: The verse commands that the earthen vessel be broken and the wooden vessel rinsed.

challenge.question: What can be understood from the repeated phrase “until evening” in verses 5–11?
answers: The uncleanness lasts forever
In many cases, uncleanness lasts until the end of the day after the required washing
The person must remain unclothed until evening
challenge.explanation: The phrase follows the instructions for washing and bathing and sets the duration of the uncleanness.

challenge.question: What special detail is given in verse 11 about contact with the man?
answers: The man must wash his hands before every contact
The person who touches him need not bathe
A person touched by him is unclean when the man has not rinsed his hands in water
challenge.explanation: Verse 11 emphasizes that if the man has not rinsed his hands, the person he touches must wash and bathe.

questions.question: What distinction between earthen and wooden vessels appears in verse 12?
answers: The earthen vessel is broken, and the wooden vessel is rinsed with water
Both are broken
The wooden vessel is burned, and the earthen vessel is washed
questions.explanation: The verse commands that the earthen vessel be broken and the wooden vessel rinsed.

answers: The uncleanness lasts forever

The person must remain unclothed until evening
questions.explanation: The phrase follows the instructions for washing and bathing and sets the duration of the uncleanness.

answers: The man must wash his hands before every contact
The person who touches him need not bathe
A person touched by him is unclean when the man has not rinsed his hands in water
questions.explanation: Verse 11 emphasizes that if the man has not rinsed his hands, the person he touches must wash and bathe.

paragraphs.title: Cleansing the man with the discharge and his offerings

easy.question: How many days must he count after being cleansed from his discharge?
answers: Seven days
Three days
Eight days
easy.explanation: The passage says that he must count seven days for his cleansing.

easy.question: What must he do with water after counting the days?
answers: Drink water
Bathe his flesh in running water
Bring water to the priest
easy.explanation: He must bathe his flesh in running water.

easy.question: What must he bring on the eighth day?
answers: A lamb and a ram
Fine flour and oil
Two turtledoves or two young pigeons
easy.explanation: On the eighth day he must take two turtledoves or two young pigeons.

medium.question: What is the correct order of the cleansing actions?
answers: Count seven days, wash his clothes, and bathe in water
Bring an offering, count seven days, and bathe
Bathe, bring an offering, and count seven days
medium.explanation: First he counts seven days, then washes his clothes and bathes in running water.

medium.question: In the phrase “cleansed of his issue,” what is he cleansed from?
answers: His home
His discharge
His offering
medium.explanation: The phrase refers to being cleansed from the bodily discharge.

medium.question: Why are the offerings brought only on the eighth day?
answers: Because the eighth day is a day of rest
Because entering the house is permitted only then
Because it follows the completion of the seven days of cleansing
medium.explanation: The eighth day comes after the seven days of counting and cleansing.

challenge.question: How does the priest divide the two birds?
answers: One is for a sin offering and one for a burnt offering
Both are for sin offerings
Both are for burnt offerings
challenge.explanation: The passage says that one is a sin offering and the other a burnt offering.

challenge.question: Where must he bring the birds before giving them to the priest?
answers: Outside the camp
To the door of the tabernacle of the congregation
To the priest’s house
challenge.explanation: He comes before the Lord at the tabernacle’s door and gives the birds to the priest.

challenge.question: Who performs the offerings according to the passage?
answers: The man with the discharge
A member of his family
The priest
challenge.explanation: The priest offers the birds and makes atonement for him.

questions.question: How does the priest divide the two birds?
answers: One is for a sin offering and one for a burnt offering
Both are for sin offerings
Both are for burnt offerings
questions.explanation: The passage says that one is a sin offering and the other a burnt offering.

questions.question: Where must he bring the birds before giving them to the priest?
answers: Outside the camp
To the door of the tabernacle of the congregation
To the priest’s house
questions.explanation: He comes before the Lord at the tabernacle’s door and gives the birds to the priest.

questions.question: Who performs the offerings according to the passage?
answers: The man with the discharge
A member of his family
The priest
questions.explanation: The priest offers the birds and makes atonement for him.

answers: Bathe his whole body in water
Only change his clothes
Offer a sacrifice immediately
easy.explanation: The verse commands him to wash all his flesh in water.

easy.question: Until when is the man unclean after bathing?
answers: Until morning
Until evening
Seven days
easy.explanation: The verse says that he is unclean until evening.

easy.question: What must be done to a garment or skin on which semen has fallen?
answers: It must be burned
It must be left in the sun
It must be washed with water
easy.explanation: The passage says that it must be washed with water.

medium.question: In the passage, what does “semen” refer to?
answers: Water spilled on the floor
The man’s reproductive fluid
Oil spread on the body
medium.explanation: The context refers to reproductive fluid coming from a man and remaining on clothing or skin.

medium.question: What do the treatment of the man and the treatment of a garment or skin have in common?
answers: Both involve water, and uncleanness lasts until evening
Both require waiting seven days
Both require an offering
medium.explanation: The man bathes, while the garment or skin is washed; in each case uncleanness lasts until evening.

medium.question: What happens when a man lies with a woman and semen goes out?
answers: Only the man becomes unclean
Only the woman must bathe
Both bathe and are unclean until evening
medium.explanation: The verse says that both of them bathe and remain unclean until evening.

challenge.question: What is the precise difference between the treatment of the man and that of the garment or skin?
answers: The man bathes his whole body, while the garment or skin is washed in water
The man is washed, while another person bathes the garment
There is no difference in the wording or action
challenge.explanation: The man washes all his flesh, while the garment or skin is washed with water.

challenge.question: What can be concluded from the fact that both the man and woman in verse 18 are unclean until evening?
answers: The woman is unclean longer than the man
The uncleanness lasts for the same period for both
Only the woman must be cleansed with water
challenge.explanation: The plural wording shows that both share the same period of uncleanness.

challenge.question: What wording in verse 18 shows that the action concerns both partners?
answers: The word “man” appears at the beginning
The word “woman” appears in the verse
The verbs “bathe” and “be unclean” are plural
challenge.explanation: The plural verbs show that the instruction and uncleanness apply to both partners.

answers: The man bathes his whole body, while the garment or skin is washed in water
The man is washed, while another person bathes the garment
There is no difference in the wording or action
questions.explanation: The man washes all his flesh, while the garment or skin is washed with water.

answers: The woman is unclean longer than the man

Only the woman must be cleansed with water
questions.explanation: The plural wording shows that both share the same period of uncleanness.

easy.question: How many days is a woman set apart during her period?
answers: Seven days
One day
Thirty days
easy.explanation: The passage says that she is set apart for seven days.

easy.question: Until when is someone who touches a woman during her period unclean?
answers: Seven days
Until evening
Until morning
easy.explanation: The verse says that the person who touches her is unclean until evening.

easy.question: What becomes unclean when the woman lies or sits on it?
answers: Only her clothing
Only the water
The bed or anything she sits on
easy.explanation: The passage says that everything on which she lies or sits becomes unclean.

medium.question: What must someone who touches the woman’s bed do?
answers: Wash his clothes, bathe in water, and remain unclean until evening
Wait seven days only
Replace the bed immediately
medium.explanation: The verse commands him to wash, bathe, and remain unclean until evening.

medium.question: What does “her separation” refer to in this passage?
answers: Her happiness
The period of her menstrual uncleanness
Her clothing
medium.explanation: The context shows that it refers to the time when she is set apart during her period.

medium.question: What happens if a man lies with the woman during her period?
answers: He is unclean only until evening
He does not become unclean
He is unclean seven days, and the bed becomes unclean
medium.explanation: The passage says that the man is unclean seven days and that the bed is unclean.

challenge.question: What is the main difference between touching the woman’s bed and lying with her during her period?
answers: Touching the bed causes uncleanness until evening, while lying with her causes seven days of uncleanness
Both always cause seven days of uncleanness
Touching the bed causes no uncleanness, but lying with her does
challenge.explanation: The touching laws specify uncleanness until evening, while lying with her causes seven days of uncleanness.

challenge.question: What detail appears in verse 23 but is not explicitly stated there as it is in verses 21–22?
answers: That the person must wash his clothes
That the person is unclean until evening, without an explicit command to wash or bathe
That the woman is set apart seven days
challenge.explanation: Verse 23 states the duration of uncleanness but does not explicitly repeat the washing and bathing commands.

challenge.question: Which is the most accurate summary of the effects described in these verses?
answers: The woman is set apart, her contact or belongings cause uncleanness, and lying with her makes the man and his bed unclean
Only the woman is unclean, and people and objects are unaffected
Everyone who touches her is unclean seven days, regardless of the contact
challenge.explanation: The verses describe uncleanness from contact, from objects she uses, and a stricter case involving intercourse.

answers: Touching the bed causes uncleanness until evening, while lying with her causes seven days of uncleanness
Both always cause seven days of uncleanness
Touching the bed causes no uncleanness, but lying with her does
questions.explanation: The touching laws specify uncleanness until evening, while lying with her causes seven days of uncleanness.

questions.explanation: Verse 23 states the duration of uncleanness but does not explicitly repeat the washing and bathing commands.

answers: The woman is set apart, her contact or belongings cause uncleanness, and lying with her makes the man and his bed unclean
Only the woman is unclean, and people and objects are unaffected
Everyone who touches her is unclean seven days, regardless of the contact
questions.explanation: The verses describe uncleanness from contact, from objects she uses, and a stricter case involving intercourse.

easy.question: What is the woman’s condition when her blood flows for many days outside her period?
answers: She is unclean
She is clean
She must immediately bring an offering
easy.explanation: The passage says that throughout the days of her discharge she is unclean.

easy.question: What is the condition of the bed and object on which she lies or sits during her discharge?
answers: They are clean
They are unclean
Only the bed is unclean
easy.explanation: The passage says that both the bed and the object become unclean.

easy.question: What must someone do after touching the unclean objects?
answers: Wait a week
Bring an offering
Wash his clothes, bathe in water, and remain unclean until evening
easy.explanation: The verse gives these instructions to anyone who touches them.

medium.question: What can be understood from comparing the woman’s discharge with her menstrual period?
answers: The uncleanness laws during the discharge are similar to those during her period
The discharge causes no uncleanness
Only the woman, not her belongings, becomes unclean
medium.explanation: The passage says that the days of her discharge are treated like the days of her period.

medium.question: In the phrase “if a woman have an issue of her blood,” what is the issue?
answers: Rest
A flow or discharge
Joy
medium.explanation: The phrase refers to blood flowing from the woman.

medium.question: What is the order of actions for someone who touched the unclean objects?
answers: Bathe, sleep, and wait a week
Bring an offering, wash, and then eat
Wash his clothes, bathe in water, and remain unclean until evening
medium.explanation: The verse lists washing clothes, bathing, and uncleanness until evening in that order.

challenge.question: What does the comparison with the woman’s period teach when the discharge lasts a long time?
answers: Uncleanness also applies when the discharge occurs outside the normal period
The discharge is clean if it lasts a long time
The woman is unclean only on the first day
challenge.explanation: The passage says that a discharge outside her period is treated like the days of her period.

challenge.question: What is emphasized by “every bed” and “whatever she sits upon”?
answers: Only the place where blood is visible becomes unclean
All the bed or object on which she lies or sits becomes unclean
Only metal objects can become unclean
challenge.explanation: The wording extends the uncleanness to the entire bed or object involved.

challenge.question: What do the words “unclean until evening” indicate about the person who touched the objects?
answers: He remains unclean forever
He becomes clean immediately
His uncleanness lasts until evening, after the required washing and bathing
challenge.explanation: The phrase limits the duration of his uncleanness to the period ending at evening.

questions.question: What does the comparison with the woman’s period teach when the discharge lasts a long time?
answers: Uncleanness also applies when the discharge occurs outside the normal period
The discharge is clean if it lasts a long time
The woman is unclean only on the first day
questions.explanation: The passage says that a discharge outside her period is treated like the days of her period.

questions.question: What is emphasized by “every bed” and “whatever she sits upon”?
answers: Only the place where blood is visible becomes unclean
All the bed or object on which she lies or sits becomes unclean
Only metal objects can become unclean
questions.explanation: The wording extends the uncleanness to the entire bed or object involved.

questions.question: What do the words “unclean until evening” indicate about the person who touched the objects?
answers: He remains unclean forever
He becomes clean immediately
His uncleanness lasts until evening, after the required washing and bathing
questions.explanation: The phrase limits the duration of his uncleanness to the period ending at evening.

easy.question: How many days must she count after the discharge stops?
answers: Seven days
Three days
Fourteen days
easy.explanation: The passage says that she must count seven days.

easy.question: To whom must she bring the two birds?
answers: The king
The priest
The judge
easy.explanation: On the eighth day she brings the birds to the priest.

easy.question: What does the priest do with the two birds?
answers: Offers both as burnt offerings
Releases both
Makes one a sin offering and the other a burnt offering
easy.explanation: The priest offers one as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering.

medium.question: What is the correct order of events?
answers: She counts seven days, is cleansed, and brings the birds on the eighth day
She brings the birds, counts seven days, and is cleansed
She is cleansed immediately and then counts seven days
medium.explanation: After the discharge stops, she counts seven days, and then comes the eighth day for the offering.

medium.question: In the phrase “cleansed of her issue,” what is she cleansed from?
answers: Her clothing
Her discharge or bleeding
Her offering
medium.explanation: The phrase refers to the bodily discharge from which she is cleansed.

medium.question: What must she do on the eighth day?
answers: Begin counting seven days again
Remain outside the camp
Take two birds and bring them to the priest
medium.explanation: On the eighth day she takes two turtledoves or young pigeons to the priest.

challenge.question: What role does each of the two birds have?
answers: One is for a sin offering and one for a burnt offering
One is for a peace offering and one for a grain offering
Both are for sin offerings
challenge.explanation: The passage distinguishes the birds by assigning one to each type of offering.

challenge.question: Who brings the birds to the priest according to the passage?
answers: The priest
The woman
Her family members
challenge.explanation: The wording says that she brings the birds to the priest.

challenge.question: What is the purpose of the priest’s action at the end of the process?
answers: To announce the beginning of the discharge
To punish the woman for her illness
To make atonement for her before the Lord for her uncleanness
challenge.explanation: The passage ends by saying that the priest makes atonement for her before the Lord.

answers: Separate themselves from uncleanness
Build a new tabernacle
Fight the nations
easy.explanation: The verse commands the Israelites to separate themselves from their uncleanness.

easy.question: What does the verse warn may happen because of uncleanness?
answers: They may leave the land
They may die in their uncleanness
They may be forbidden to eat bread
easy.explanation: The verse warns that they must not die in their uncleanness.

easy.question: What might the Israelites defile?
answers: The sea
The mountains
The tabernacle
easy.explanation: The verse warns that they could defile the Lord’s tabernacle among them.

medium.question: What is the connection between separating from uncleanness and the tabernacle?
answers: Separation protects the holiness of the tabernacle
Separation keeps the tabernacle away from the people
Separation replaces the tabernacle
medium.explanation: The command is connected with preventing the tabernacle from being defiled.

medium.question: In “separate the children of Israel from their uncleanness,” what does “separate” mean?
answers: Count the Israelites
Bring the Israelites closer
Keep the Israelites away
medium.explanation: The command means to set the Israelites apart or keep them away from uncleanness.

medium.question: What may happen if the Israelites are not careful about their uncleanness?
answers: They may defile the tabernacle and die in their uncleanness
They must build a new city
They receive a new role in the tabernacle
medium.explanation: The verse warns of both defiling the tabernacle and dying in uncleanness.

challenge.question: What can be understood from “my tabernacle that is among them”?
answers: The tabernacle is located among the Israelites
The tabernacle is outside the land of Israel
The tabernacle belongs only to the priests

challenge.question: What does “that they die not in their uncleanness” emphasize?
answers: Uncleanness is unrelated to human conduct
Avoiding uncleanness prevents a serious consequence
Death is the way to become clean

The tabernacle must be kept away from the Israelites
